Why Wake Forest?
Our Mission is to train and mentor future leaders in research, teaching, and innovation in service to humanity. This embodies our vital role as an engine of discovery that fuels the nation’s scholarly and creative enterprise. We strongly believe there is room for all of us to be successful. To that end, our goal is to cultivate a culture that is team-focused, with a primary emphasis on creating a supportive and inclusive atmosphere that allows all students to feel sustained by their peers, faculty mentors, collaborators, and our administrative team. On the school of medicine campus, our students have the rare opportunity to see our Mission impact patient care through their work. Students on our campus are surrounded by an environment that is deeply committed to improving the health of our community, nation, and world.
Key Features of Wake Forest’s Biomedical Graduate Education
Personalized Education
With approximately 425 master and doctoral biomedical graduate students and ~200 School of Medicine-based graduate faculty, students receive plenty of one-on-one time with their mentors and other faculty.
Our Student Body
Our students come from approximately 35 states and 27 countries.
Successful Career Outcomes
The rigorous educational foundation provided at Wake Forest, as well as the strong academic and career advising in our system, produces graduates that are career ready on graduation day. Graduates of Wake Forest’s biomedical graduate programs are found in careers in academics, industry, government, and other professional schools. Post-graduation success is an expectation and guiding principle at Wake Forest.
Embedded Ethics Training
Producing graduates with a strong sense of integrity and professionalism is an important tenant of a Wake Forest education. All biomedical graduate students undergo extensive, and practical, training to ensure that ethical considerations are explored deeply in a more consequence-free environment. In addition, the discussion of ethics are folded into program curricula to ensure that it’s never an afterthought.
Dynamic Research Opportunities
With a multitude of ongoing translational studies, the research culture on the school of medicine campus is highly collaborative. This offers students the opportunity to learn multiple research approaches and diversify their research portfolio; in essence, our student’s research often represents a bridge between laboratories in pursuit of improved patient health.

About the Biomedical Graduate Program Office Administration
Life for Students in Biomedical Graduate Programs
Admissions
Undergraduate seniors and graduates of accredited U.S. colleges and universities or recognized foreign institutions may apply for admission. Undergraduates must complete their degree requirements prior to matriculation. The Graduate School also accepts applications from holders of the MD, DDS, or DVM degrees, or from candidates for these degrees who will have satisfactorily completed the prescribed medical curriculum prior to matriculation. All applicants should have superior records. This requirement is usually interpreted as at least a B (3.0 GPA or greater) average or standing in the upper quarter of the class or both.
